newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early Asia oil sags, Korea shops in W.Africa, Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Early Asia oil sags, Korea shops in W.Africa, Yemen.

text.p: Futures prices sagged in early Asia with regional physical markets still muted by limited refinery needs. But a persistently lean Brent/Dubai spread saw Korean refiners dealing in dated related grades from West Africa and Yemen, traders said.

Notional cash Brent values for August were pegged by brokers at $17.95/18.05. The 15 cent drop from a day earlier followed weekly data showing bearish stockbuilds in U.S. gasoline and distillate inventories.

Brent/Dubai deals continued to dominate Asian oil markets, with at least six deals done in the last two days, as movers of dated East of Suez related grades sought hedge providers to cover their exposure.

A 900,000 barrel parcel of August Masila was heard sold by a Korean refiner to a U.S. trader at OSP plus 15/20 cts, with the buyer selling a September Brent/Dubai to another U.S. trader at $1.09. A similar deal was heard at $1.05 from a U.S. trader to a European major.
Another Korean refiner was widely believed to have picked up a 900,000 barrel Djeno from a Congo equity producer.
Japan refiners, still plagued with high product inventories, felt left out of the action.
"We'd like to be taking advantage of these opportunities for West African barrels, but we just do not have the room for spot barrels at this point," said one trader.
